title: Corned Beef Hash
subtitle: A British stovetop fry of tinned corned beef and potato
excerpt: Tinned corned beef and cooked potato fried in one pan until crisp and golden at the edges. Quick, cheap and ready in under half an hour.
sourceNotes: British tinned-corned-beef tradition, adapted for a standard large frying pan on the hob.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Boil and cool the potatoes ahead of time. Fry the hash fresh to order.

content.text: British corned beef hash is a simple stovetop fry using tinned corned beef and leftover or freshly boiled potato. The key is to leave it alone in the pan so the underside forms a crust. Serve with a fried egg on top if you like.
Heat the oil in the frying pan over a medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 6 minutes until soft and starting to colour.
Add the diced potato and press down lightly into the pan. Cook without stirring for 5 minutes so a crust forms on the bottom.
Break the corned beef over the potato in rough chunks. Add the worcestershire sauce if using. Season with plenty of black pepper.
Stir everything together to combine. Press the mixture down firmly with the spatula into an even layer.
Cook for another 8 to 10 minutes, pressing and turning every few minutes, until the hash is deeply golden and crisp in places.
Serve straight from the pan, topped with a fried egg if you like.

items.symptom: The hash is sticking and burning.
items.cause: The pan was not hot enough at the start or had too little oil.
items.fix: Use a generous amount of oil and let it heat up fully before adding the onion.

items.symptom: The hash is pale and soft with no crust.
items.cause: The pan was too cool or the hash was stirred too often.
items.fix: Turn up the heat slightly and press the hash flat. Leave it alone for 5 minutes at a time.

items.symptom: The corned beef turns to mush.
items.cause: It was added too early and overworked.
items.fix: Add the corned beef after the potato has coloured. Break it in loosely and do not over-stir.
